fact: The Universal Service Fund's Integrated Annual Report 2025 carries the Fund's first audited financial statements, for the 18 months to 31 December 2025, per this catalogue page; the amounts collected and spent are not stated on the page.
The Ministry of Information and Communication Technology contributed N$115 million over three years towards the Universal Service Fund, per CRAN's report for the year to 31 March 2025.

The Fund was established under section 56 of the Communications Act with levy regulations finalised, was officially launched on 19 March 2025 with N$115 million from the Ministry over three years, and its first bidding round allocated almost N$31 million of capital subsidies to MTC for nine sites.
The government allocated N$145 million over three years as seed funding for the Universal Service Fund, announced by the Minister of ICT at the launch.
At the Fund's launch the minister announced the state seed funding, and CRAN had already disbursed a N$31 million subsidy to MTC for nine network sites.

Regulations made under section 56(2) of the Communications Act impose a universal service levy on every licensee of up to 0.5 percent of annual turnover, with a N$500 minimum, payable into the Universal Service Fund and effective on gazettal.

CRAN's report for the year to 31 March 2024 records a commitment of N$115 million over three years from the Government of Namibia to build towers in unserved areas under the universal service regulations.

The Ministry of Information and Communication Technology's 2026/27 budget is N$639.2 million (N$625.7 million operational, N$13.6 million development projects), as presented by its Acting Executive Director; no event date given, so the published date is used.

CRAN's Universal Service Fund paid for a project: on 9 April 2026 Telecom Namibia and CRAN signed the Phase 2 agreement, a subsidy of N$9,796,650 to build rural Radio Access Network sites; the document does not name the law that set up the fund.

CRAN's Universal Service Fund Phase 2 awarded MTC N$32.3 million for nine network solutions including 10 towers in underserved areas; the award date is not given, so the date MTC confirmed it is used, and the document does not name the law.

The Villager reports the Universal Service Fund has provided 16 schools and four clinics with uncapped Wi-Fi and one tower in Kavango East, and that CRAN uses it to prioritise regions below 80% 4G coverage; no date is given for the Wi-Fi or tower, so the document's published date is used.

CRAN states that new telecommunications towers at Epinga (launched 19 November 2025) and Ehomba (launched 30 January 2026) were built under the Universal Service Fund; the document does not name the law or amounts.

ITWeb reports ICT minister Emma Theofelus distributed 100 mobile phones paid for from the Universal Service Fund to top learners at the Ehomba tower launch in Kunene, the weekend before 2 February 2026.
